title: Finite-free algebra resolutions from base-ring pseudo-coherence
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $B$ a possibly noncommutative unital $A$-algebra (the image of $A$ lies in the centre of $B$). Suppose $B$ is finite free as an $A$-module, that is, $B\cong A^{\oplus r}$ as $A$-modules for some finite $r\geq0$. Let $M$ be an object of the unbounded derived category of right $B$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If the underlying object $\operatorname{Res}_A M\in D(A)$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], then $M$ is isomorphic in $D(\operatorname{Mod}\!\text{-}B)$ to a bounded-above cochain complex $F^\bullet$ with each $F^i$ a finite free right $B$-module.

proof.text: Choose a complex $K^\bullet$ of right $B$-modules representing $M$. By pseudo-coherence its restriction to $A$ is isomorphic to a bounded-above finite-free $A$-complex $E^\bullet$. Choose $b\in\mathbf Z$ with $E^i=0$ for $i>b$; hence $H^i(K)=0$ for $i>b$. Restriction of scalars keeps the underlying additive groups, kernels and images, so this is also vanishing as right $B$-modules. We construct, for $n=b+1,b,b-1,\ldots$, a finite-free right $B$-complex $F_{\geq n}$ supported in $[n,b]$ and a chain map $\alpha_n:F_{\geq n}\to K$ inducing isomorphisms on $H^i$ for $i>n$ and a surjection for $i=n$. At $n=b+1$ take the zero complex and zero map. Each extension will keep all previously chosen terms and maps.

source.place: Tag 0CSF, lemma-pseudo-coherent-over-algebra, proof; upper bound and descending-induction invariant; start with the zero complex

proof.text: Suppose the stage $n$ is constructed. Form $T=C(\alpha_n)$ with $T^i=K^i\oplus F_{\geq n}^{i+1}$ and $d_T(x,y)=(d_Kx+\alpha_n y,-d_Fy)$. In the long exact sequence of its cone triangle, for $i\geq n$ the map $H^i(F_{\geq n})\to H^i(K)$ is surjective and the map $H^{i+1}(F_{\geq n})\to H^{i+1}(K)$ is injective. Exactness therefore gives $H^i(T)=0$ for every $i\geq n$. These statements hold over $B$ and after restriction to $A$.

source.place: Tag 0CSF, lemma-pseudo-coherent-over-algebra, proof; cone and its cohomology vanishing

proof.text: As an $A$-complex $F_{\geq n}$ is bounded finite free: if $F^i\cong B^{\oplus s_i}$, the given $A$-basis of $B$ gives $F^i\cong A^{\oplus rs_i}$. Its identity is an $n$-pseudo-coherent witness. The brutal truncation $E_{\geq n-1}\to E$, followed by the derived isomorphism to $\operatorname{Res}_A K$, witnesses $(n-1)$-pseudo-coherence of $\operatorname{Res}_A K$: cohomology is unchanged above $n-1$, and removing incoming boundaries makes the map surjective in degree $n-1$. Restriction preserves the displayed cone formula and hence gives a distinguished triangle over $A$. Apply [lem-sc-cone-pseudo-coherent] with its parameter $m=n-1$ to obtain $(n-1)$-pseudo-coherence of $\operatorname{Res}_A T$. Its cohomology vanishes above $n-1$ by Step 2, so [lem-sc-finite-cohomology] gives a finite set of $A$-module generators of $H^{n-1}(T)$.

source.place: Tag 0CSF, lemma-pseudo-coherent-over-algebra, proof; finite base-ring obstruction group, using Tags 064R and 064S

proof.text: Choose cycles $z_1,\ldots,z_s\in T^{n-1}$ lifting those $A$-generators. They generate cohomology also as a right $B$-module: an $A$-linear expression $\sum_j a_j[z_j]$ equals $\sum_j[z_j]\iota(a_j)$ under restriction through the central scalar map $\iota:A\to B$. Set $F^{n-1}=B^{\oplus s}$ and define the right $B$-linear map $\beta:F^{n-1}\to T^{n-1}$ by its basis images $z_j$. Then $d_T\beta=0$, and the induced map to $H^{n-1}(T)$ is surjective. Since $T^{n-1}=K^{n-1}\oplus F^n$, write $\beta=(a,-d)$. The cycle equation says $d_Ka=\alpha_n^n d$ and $d_F^n d=0$. Thus adjoining $F^{n-1}$ with differential $d$ and chain-map component $a$ produces $\alpha_{n-1}:F_{\geq n-1}\to K$, keeping all higher data. An empty generating set gives $s=0$ and is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0CSF, lemma-pseudo-coherent-over-algebra, proof; lift a finite set of obstruction generators and read off the two components of beta

proof.text: Let $T'=C(\alpha_{n-1})$. For $i\geq n-1$ the terms $T'^i$, their outgoing differentials, and their cycles agree with those of $T$. The only change affecting their boundaries is in degree $n-1$: $T'^{n-2}=K^{n-2}\oplus F^{n-1}$, and its differential is $(u,v)\mapsto(d_Ku,0)+\beta(v)$. Consequently $H^{n-1}(T')=H^{n-1}(T)/\operatorname{im}(\overline\beta)=0$, while $H^i(T')=H^i(T)=0$ for $i\geq n$. The long exact cone sequence now gives that $H^i(\alpha_{n-1})$ is an isomorphism for $i\geq n$ (both adjacent cone groups vanish) and is surjective for $i=n-1$ (the following cone group vanishes). This proves exactly the induction invariant for the next stage.

source.place: Tag 0CSF, lemma-pseudo-coherent-over-algebra, proof; verification of the improved approximation, by the explicit cone boundaries

proof.text: Take the terms, differentials and chain-map components fixed by this descending recursion, obtaining $F^\bullet$ and $\alpha:F^\bullet\to K^\bullet$. Every relation $d^{i+1}d^i=0$ and $d_K\alpha^i=\alpha^{i+1}d^i$ already holds at stage $n=i$. Each term is finite free over $B$, and $F^i=0$ for $i>b$. For a fixed $j$, stage $n=j-1$ has already fixed all three terms and both differentials computing $H^j(F)$, and $H^j(\alpha_{j-1})$ is an isomorphism. Subsequent stages change none of these data, so $H^j(\alpha)$ is an isomorphism for every $j$. Hence $\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism and becomes an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}\!\text{-}B)$, as required.
